Project integration session with timeline review and launch targets

Database and API integration context

  • Straw provided endpoint keys, database users, and table access credentials in chat.
  • CMS updates ensure country, city, and state data flow correctly for player records.
  • Address validation updates deployed this week will resolve messy data in location fields.

Survey tracking requirements

  • Salesforce requires storing completion status and dates for both survey 1 and survey 2.
  • Second survey completion typically occurs within 72 hours post-signup.
  • Only binary completion tracking is needed in Salesforce rather than progress percentages.

Signup workflow and UI decisions

  • Attribution details belong in the standard header bar across all record statuses.
  • List views default to active records and sort by descending creation date.
  • Date validation blocks future entries and ensures wager dates follow signup dates.
  • A dedicated full-width notes section supports catchall note-taking in the signup log.
  • Operations workflows require a button to undo fraud flags and manage review statuses.
  • Signup headers display partner short codes to enable quick identification.

View options and data export decisions

  • Kanban views are excluded from phase one pending future user feedback collection.
  • Table views align closely with existing spreadsheet layouts and support CSV exports.

VIP process requirements

  • Manual VIP signup creation requires restricted user access via specific permission sets.

VIP player and signup management

  • Designated operators manually create VIP player and signup records directly in Salesforce.
  • VIP signups bypass the pending state and default directly to in-progress status.
  • Email addresses serve as unique identifiers for CMS integration while external IDs remain blank.
  • Referrer records include a toggle indicating VIP status to support diverse signup types.
  • VIP-exclusive tracking links are excluded from the CMS flow and utilized directly within Salesforce.
  • Crown icons appear next to VIP player and signup names across application list views.

Deal naming conventions and data validation

  • Multi-state deal naming conventions incorporate specific regional prefixes for Canadian and US state markets.
  • High-volume representatives conduct data validation testing on SLC data for Alex and Andy.
  • Phase 1 development focuses on fine-tuning core components following the completion of major features.

Project timeline and launch planning

  • The team targets a November 1 launch, requiring build completion by October 9.
  • Kobi Kunasekaran takes vacation leave from October 12 to October 23.
  • Backend payouts and referral discovery sessions align with the aggressive phase 1 schedule.

Summary

Project integration session with timeline review and launch targets

CMS Data and Survey Updates
Address validation is being implemented this week to clean up messy data fields. Survey completion statuses will be tracked in Salesforce.

VIP Workflow and Signup Configuration
Manual VIP signups will automatically start in an in-progress status and link to existing deals. A crown icon will indicate VIP status in Salesforce lists.

Project Timeline and Launch Targets
Team maintained a November 1st launch target with discovery sessions scheduled immediately. Design and scoping must be completed over the next 2.5 weeks.

Decisions

Aligned

  • Salesforce survey completion tracking fields First and second survey completion status and dates will be stored in Salesforce.
  • Survey completion status tracking configuration Salesforce will track only survey completion status rather than percentage complete.
  • Attribution details in record headers Attribution details will be displayed in the standard header bar across all record statuses.
  • Signup list default view settings The signup list view will default to all active items sorted by descending created date.
  • Proof status and completion placement Proof status and completion fields will be relocated to the far right of the interface header.
  • Date field future entry restrictions System validation will prevent signup, deposit, and first wager dates from being set to future dates.
  • Signup log notes section layout A separate full-width section will be created for notes within the signup log.
  • Fraud review status action button A dedicated action button will be implemented for managing fraud review statuses in the operations view.
  • Kanban view phase one removal The kanban view option will be hidden for the phase one launch pending further feedback.
  • Manual signup record creation permissions Manual creation of signup records will be restricted to designated operations users via a specific permission set.
  • VIP player regular signup capabilities VIP players are permitted to perform regular signups, and users must be able to specify whether a signup is a VIP signup.
  • Status workflow for manual VIP signups Manual VIP signups bypass the pending state and automatically start in progress before being moved to completed or archived.
  • Referrer VIP toggle and flexibility Referrers include a VIP toggle to support both VIP and non-VIP signups under a single unique referrer record.
  • Crown icon indicator for VIP status A crown icon indicator is implemented for VIP status on both player and signup records and lists.
  • Multi-state deal naming conventions Multi-state deal naming conventions retain the multi label unless broken out by specific regional markets.

Details

  • Sandbox Access and CMS Data Updates: Emily Vandenberg and Strahinja Vladetic discussed sandbox access and Postgres querying credentials, which Strahinja Vladetic shared in the chat. Emily Vandenberg explained that country, city, and state data were previously missing because of a new Content Management System (CMS) that did not pass those fields through, but stated that the issue is now resolved for future entries (00:00:02) (00:09:51). Additionally, Emily Vandenberg noted that address validation is being implemented this week to clean up messy data fields (00:04:14).
  • Survey Tracking and Salesforce Integration: Emily Vandenberg, Kobi Kunasekaran, Lena Ceniccola, and Joyce Kiddell discussed tracking survey completion statuses and dates in Salesforce for both initial and second surveys (00:05:06). Strahinja Vladetic noted that the second survey typically completes within 72 hours post-signup (00:06:12). Kobi Kunasekaran committed to creating the necessary fields today, and they will work with Strahinja Vladetic to ensure proper data tracking (00:07:45).
  • Deal Status and Affiliate Links Payload: Kobi Kunasekaran and Strahinja Vladetic reviewed the V2 affiliate links payload and deal statuses such as active, inactive, pause, close, review required, and replace (00:09:51). Strahinja Vladetic agreed to update the payload documentation message in the chat and adjust validation on deal status fields to accommodate potential new statuses like retired (00:11:10).
  • Signup Flow User Interface and Default Lists: Emily Vandenberg, Joyce Kiddell, Lena Ceniccola, and Kobi Kunasekaran reviewed the signup flow user interface, agreeing to display attribution details in the header across all status types (00:15:11). They agreed that the signup list should default to "all active" items sorted by descending created date (00:17:19). Kobi Kunasekaran explained that Salesforce defaults the initial view to "recently viewed" due to out-of-the-box system limitations, requiring users to manually pin their preferred list during onboarding (00:19:13).
  • Signup Flow Header and Partner Code Details: Emily Vandenberg, Lena Ceniccola, and Kobi Kunasekaran discussed rearranging header fields, agreeing to move proof status and completion to the far right and to surface the partner short code and deal name to help track specific deal requirements (00:21:07). Lena Ceniccola emphasized that exposing partner short codes allows operations staff to verify that players are assigned to the correct deals (00:26:13).

  • Signup Flow Date Validations and Notes Section: Emily Vandenberg, Kobi Kunasekaran, and Lena Ceniccola discussed date fields in the signup log, noting that signup dates were prepopulating from click dates. They agreed to leave the signup date blank by default and implement validation rules preventing users from entering future dates for signup, deposit, and first wager fields, as well as ensuring deposit and wager dates do not precede the signup date (00:30:15). They also agreed to add a dedicated notes section (00:34:59).
  • Referral Creation and Fraud Review Actions: Emily Vandenberg, Kobi Kunasekaran, Lena Ceniccola, and Joyce Kiddell discussed referral creation workflows, noting that referral types and payout automation need verification (00:36:08). For fraud reviews, Emily Vandenberg and Joyce Kiddell requested a simplified button to reverse or update fraud flags rather than requiring manual editing through multiple menus, which Kobi Kunasekaran agreed to set up (00:40:51).
  • Table View Customization and Kanban View Deferral: Emily Vandenberg, Kobi Kunasekaran, and Lena Ceniccola discussed optimizing the table view to better mirror existing spreadsheets, confirming that CSV exports should be enabled (00:43:49) (00:45:44). Kobi Kunasekaran outlined column limitations in split views, and they agreed to hide the Kanban view for phase one since it is not fully optimized for user adoption (00:43:49) (00:52:11).

  • VIP Workflow and Manual Signup Permissions: Joyce Kiddell, Emily Vandenberg, Lena Ceniccola, and Kobi Kunasekaran discussed the VIP process, which requires manual player creation and tracking (00:53:07). Kobi Kunasekaran confirmed they can restore the "new signup" button and restrict its visibility to authorized operations personnel using a Salesforce permission set (00:55:46).

  • VIP Signup Record Creation and Status Flow: Joyce Kiddell and Emily Vandenberg discussed the manual creation process for VIP player records and signups, noting that designated users like Andy and Ally will create these records since volume is relatively low at about 30 signups per month (00:57:36) (01:00:56). Lena Ceniccola confirmed that VIP players can also perform regular signups (00:58:48). For tracking, Joyce Kiddell and Kobi Kunasekaran agreed that there will be no pending state for VIP signups; records will automatically start in an in-progress status upon creation and can later be moved to completed or archived by users (01:00:02). Kobi Kunasekaran noted that manual signups can be linked to existing deals (01:00:56).
  • External Player ID and Email Identification: Emily Vandenberg raised the question of whether the player ID received from the CMS should remain blank for manual VIP signups. Kobi Kunasekaran explained that since these players do not use the agency survey flow, the external ID can be left blank while Salesforce maintains its own internal player ID (01:01:57). Furthermore, Kobi Kunasekaran noted that the primary email address is unique and will serve as the identifier for any downstream CMS updates, and Joyce Kiddell confirmed that VIPs must remain searchable in lists such as redeposit eligibility (01:02:50).
  • VIP Referrer Configuration: Joyce Kiddell stated that a VIP toggle is required for referrer records, and Kobi Kunasekaran confirmed that commission rates remain the same without a differing payout matrix. When Kobi Kunasekaran asked if referrers would be exclusively marked as VIP, Joyce Kiddell and Lena Ceniccola agreed to leave the option open so that VIP referrers can also handle non-VIP signups (01:03:55).
  • VIP Links and CMS Exclusion: Joyce Kiddell brought up that specific links are exclusively used for VIPs and need to be attributed to the link while being excluded from the CMS flow. Kobi Kunasekaran confirmed that the CMS does not require these links and that the exclusion can be implemented. Joyce Kiddell explained that users will manually go into Salesforce and send these links directly to users instead of surfacing them through the website (01:05:05).
  • Signup Screen Flow, Required Fields, and Proof Collection: Kobi Kunasekaran proposed utilizing a custom screen flow for VIP signups to provide a restrictive view that only shows relevant fields rather than the full off-suit view containing fraud details (01:07:40). Following confirmation from Lena Ceniccola and Emily Vandenberg, Kobi Kunasekaran verified that standard requirements, including the collection of VIP screenshots and proofs alongside attribution data, remain mandatory before marking a signup as complete (01:08:36).

  • Visual Indicators for VIP Players and Signups: Lena Ceniccola suggested using a crown icon to clearly indicate VIP status, and Emily Vandenberg and Kobi Kunasekaran agreed to implement this visual indicator next to player names and signup list views in Salesforce (01:11:05).
  • Project Timeline, Data Validation, and Deal Naming Conventions: Kobi Kunasekaran and Emily Vandenberg discussed prioritizing signup feedback clean-up over the next one to two weeks, while straw runs data validation on SLC data for Alex and Andy (01:13:45). Regarding multi-state deals, Kobi Kunasekaran addressed a naming convention discrepancy where documentation specified "multistate" as a prefix, whereas standard naming uses region-specific prefixes such as Canadian provinces or US state prefixes (e.g., Proline Direct Casino) (01:15:02). Emily Vandenberg and Lena Ceniccola agreed with standardizing the naming structure to region-specific or multi formats (01:16:30). Kobi Kunasekaran also noted they are finalizing phase one hour breakdowns and reviewing major project components (01:17:47).

  • Representative Filtering Views for Signups and Redeposits: Kobi Kunasekaran highlighted that current list views lack an easy partner-filtering mechanism for redeposits, suggesting that users could rely on custom or quick filters by partner (such as GDC). Emily Vandenberg compared this to existing spreadsheet filtering habits (01:19:54). Kobi Kunasekaran and Emily Vandenberg agreed to defer an immediate solution until redeposit workflows are built out, as optimized workflows may handle filtering in a different location (01:21:05) (01:23:10).

  • Discovery Sessions, Vacation Schedules, and November 1st Launch Target: Kobi Kunasekaran informed the team of an upcoming vacation from October 12th to October 23rd, emphasizing that necessary design and scoping must be completed over the next two and a half weeks (01:24:15). Emily Vandenberg and Kobi Kunasekaran maintained a November 1st launch target, though Waleed Alasadi noted that building must finish by October 9th for a November 2nd go-live. To stay on track, Emily Vandenberg and Kobi Kunasekaran agreed to schedule remaining discovery sessions for referrals and payouts immediately (01:25:08) (01:28:14). Kobi Kunasekaran will present trade-offs between custom builds and out-of-the-box features to determine what is necessary for launch versus what can be deferred post-launch (01:29:10).
